en: One Volume of Liturgical Texts for Repentance With all reverence, I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem. [This offering of] various flowers,
incense, and food— may these clouds of fragrant flowers transform and fill the worlds of the ten directions.
They make offerings to all the manifested Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, as well as the countless Śrāvakas who receive these clouds of incense and flowers.
They perceive that the light of the Radiant Terrace is made by the Buddhas through boundless realms, boundlessly and immeasurably.
They made offerings and paid homage to all together while reciting the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra:
"The Tathāgata’s wondrous form and body are peerless and incomparable in the world; they are inconceivable."
Therefore, I now pay homage to the form of the Tathāgata;
his inexhaustible wisdom is likewise so.
All phenomena abide eternally; at this time, I take refuge in and pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem, extolling the virtues of the Buddha.
The Buddha possesses the thirty-two marks and eighty secondary signs;
he is titled the One Who Has Attained the Buddha-way to deliver sentient beings throughout the three realms.
Homage to the Tathāgata Sumerudīpaprabhāsa in the eastern direction, and to all the Buddhas of the ten directions and everywhere.
Homage to the Tathāgata Vipaśyin and all Buddhas, such as the Seven Buddhas of the Past.
Homage to the Tathāgata Samantaprabha and all Buddhas, such as the Fifty-three Buddhas.
Homage to the Tathāgata Śubhavyūha of the East and all Buddhas, such as the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions.
Homage to all Buddhas, such as the Tathāgata Kanakamuni and the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa;
homage to all Buddhas, such as the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and the thirty-five Buddhas;
homage to all Buddhas, such as the Tathāgata Akṣobhya of the eastern quarter and the fifteen thousand Buddhas.
Homage to the twenty-five Buddhas, beginning with the Tathāgata Saṃbhavagarbha, and to all other Buddhas.
Homage to the Buddha Dharmaprabhāsaviśuddhavikrāntapadmaprabha.

Homage to the Tathāgata Gaganaguṇaviśuddhasūkṣmajālasamantacakṣuḥsuvibhaktakusumatejorājendragarbha. Homage to the Tathāgata Padmottaragandhārcisamudgataratnavyūhagarbha. Homage to the Tathāgata Gandhottamakūṭa. Homage to the Tathāgata Sarvavyūhapratimaṇḍitānantāvabhāsatejorāja. Homage to the Tathāgata Candra-sūrya-prabhāsa-praṇidhāna-vyūha-vikurvita-dharmadhātu-niḥsaraṇa-āvaraṇarāja. Homage to all the Buddhas.

Homage to the Tathāgata King of the Universal Manifestation of the Sun, Moon, Radiant Flower-Vow Jewel Lotus, Whose Body is as Firm as Vajra, Whose Eyes are Like Vairocana and Unobstructed, Who Perfectly Illuminates the Ten Directions and Shines Light Upon All Beings—

namely, the gods of the higher realms, the nāgas, the eight classes of spirits, sovereigns, lords of men, teachers, monks, parents, donors from the ten directions, and all sentient beings throughout the boundless dharma-realm.
I vow to sever and abandon all obstacles to knowledge; I take refuge and repent. With a sincere heart, I repent:
the entire ocean of karmic obstacles arises from the production of expectations.
If one wishes to repent, [one must eliminate these expectations].
Sitting upright, contemplate the true nature of reality;
all transgressions are like frost and dew, which the sun of wisdom can gradually dissolve.
Therefore, one should with a sincere heart diligently repent for the offenses of the six sense organs.

I repent and take refuge by bowing in homage to the Triple Gem. With a sincere heart, I make this vow: "May we, in every birth, encounter these Buddhas, and in every lifetime, constantly hear the teaching of liberation."
With great vows, they impartially deliver all sentient beings,
ultimately accomplishing the unsurpassed path;
they make this aspiration and take refuge by bowing in worship to the Triple Gem.
Recite this verse to make a vow: "May these merits extend universally to all;
may we and all sentient beings together attain the path to Buddhahood.
Addressing the assembly, listen to the Verse on Impermanence at Dusk: "The sun in the west is fading away."
The defilements are as numerous as motes of dust;
when the time for old age, sickness, and death arrives,
we cannot remain together even as we gaze upon one another.
Moment by moment the years are driven away,
like a fish in scanty water;
I exhort all those who practice the Path.
Through diligent study, one reaches fearlessness.
I address the assembly: listen as I recite the verses on impermanence for the first watch of the night.
The ocean of birth and death is bottomless and its shores are boundless; it is the sea of afflictions.
The boat for crossing over suffering has not yet arrived;
why do you delight in sleep?
You must awaken from this slumber!
Do not let sleep shroud the mind;
through courageous and diligent exertion, the path to enlightenment will become natural.
Homage to the Buddha Vairocana!
Homage to Vairocana Buddha; homage to Śākyamuni Buddha;
homage to the Buddha Kuśalamati of the eastern quarter.
Homage to the Buddha Aśoka-prāpta in the southeast.
Homage to the Buddha Candana in the south.
Homage to the Buddha Ratna-jaya in the southwest.
Homage to the Buddha Amitābha of the western direction.
Homage to the Buddha Padmottara of the northwestern direction.
Homage to the Buddha Lakṣmīṃkara of the northern direction.
Homage to the Buddha Trailokyavijaya in the northeast.
Homage to the Buddha Sarvārthasiddha above.
Homage to the Buddha Adhastādvidyutprabha below.
Homage to the Honored Buddha Maitreya, who shall descend to be born in the future; homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time—past, present, and future;
homage to the physical relics, images, and immeasurable jeweled stupas;
homage to the twelve divisions of the honored sutras, the profound treasury of the Dharma.
Homage to the assembly of all great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas;
homage to all the worthy and holy ones, the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; homage with all reverence to the eight classes of beings and all benevolent divine kings;
homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem; and homage to the teachers of the past and present, who are forever the leaders of the Way.
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem for the sake of emperors and kings whose holy transformation shall be inexhaustible;
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem for the sake of crown princes and various kings whose blessings shall extend through ten thousand generations;
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem for the sake of teachers, monks, parents, and spiritual friends.
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem for the sake of the donors of the ten directions, that their six perfections may be fulfilled.
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem for the sake of sentient beings suffering, that they may all be freed from suffering.
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem for the sake of the civil and military officials, that their emoluments and positions may remain constant.
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem for the peace and stability of the nation and the perpetual turning of the Wheel of Dharma;
I pay homage to the eternally abiding Triple Gem for the sake of all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm.
I prostrate to the Buddha and repent, repenting with a sincere heart: there is nothing that the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions do not fully know.
I have now fully confessed and turned away from the three evil realms;
these three groups of three make nine types,
all arising from the three afflictions.
I now repent for all the transgressions committed by this present body as well as those of previous lives.
Regarding the karmic retributions that ought to be experienced within the three evil realms, I pray that they may instead be received by this present body,
so that I shall never again enter the evil realms throughout my life.

Having accepted the confession, I take refuge and pay homage to the Triple Gem. With a sincere heart, I entreat all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions who are currently dwelling in the attainment of enlightenment:
"I pray that you turn the Wheel of Dharma to bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings."
If all Buddhas of the ten directions wish to relinquish their lives,
I now prostrate with my head in homage, entreating them to remain for a long time.
Having made this entreaty by taking refuge and prostrating to the Triple Gem, I wholeheartedly rejoice in all merit derived from acts of giving.
The observance of precepts, the cultivation of dhyāna,
and wisdom arise from body, speech, and mind.
All those currently training in the three vehicles do so accordingly.
Those who are fully endowed with the One Vehicle—
the immeasurable multitudes of humans and devas, and the assembly of those possessing merit—
shall all rejoice and, following my command, pay homage to the Triple Gem and wholeheartedly dedicate [the merit].
May all the meritorious deeds I have performed be combined for the sake of liberating all sentient beings;
I dedicate them solely toward the Buddha-way.
One should likewise repent of transgressions, offer exhortations, rejoice in merit, and dedicate that merit toward Bodhi.
Dedicate this by taking refuge and prostrating to the Triple Gem, and with a sincere heart make this vow:
"May all sentient beings alike resolve to attain Bodhicitta,
and may their minds constantly keep in mind all the Buddhas of the ten directions."
I humbly pray that all sentient beings may forever shatter all afflictions and clearly perceive the Buddha’s lineage, just as the Buddha Wondrous Virtue did.
Having made this vow, I take refuge and pay homage to the Triple Gem. I address the assembly: please listen as I recite the Verse of Purity for the Early Morning.
Desiring to attain the bliss of nirvana,
one should train in the dharma of a śramaṇa;
clothing and food are merely for sustaining the physical life.
All you assembly, both refined and coarse,
today at the dawn of the morning, having purified yourselves,
each should maintain the six recollections.
With all reverence,
I take refuge in the Buddha.
May all beings embody and study the Great Way, giving rise to the realization of impermanence.
Taking refuge in the Dharma,
I vow that all sentient beings may enter deeply into the treasury of the sutras, their wisdom as vast as the ocean.
Taking refuge in the Sangha...
May all beings govern the great assemblies with total unimpededness.
May all beings purify their three karmas and uphold the Buddha’s teachings.
Homage to all worthy and holy ones.
Recorded on the twenty-second day of the fourth month in the second year of the Xiande era, the year of Yimao (1035 CE), by the monk Xin Yuan of Daxuan Temple.
